svg.title: The very essence of romance is uncertainty.

text.tspan: Everyday English - C2 - 2026/10/28 - Quote - 01

svg.title: Heart-shaped decorations accompany a comic argument about romance.

text.tspan: Heart-shaped decorations accompany a comic argument about romance.
The very essence of romance is
uncertainty.
Algernon Moncrieff (fictional character) · Oscar Wilde · The Importance of Being Earnest, Act
I · Published 1899 · First performed 1895
Jack has come to town hoping to propose to Gwendolen.
Algernon distinguishes the excitement of being in love from the
definite business of making a proposal. If the proposal is
accepted, he argues, the uncertainty disappears and the
excitement is over. His remark is witty precisely because it
turns a conventional romantic destination into a
disappointment. The exchange reveals a character enjoying
his own cleverness; it does not establish a universal rule about
relationships.
Very intensifies essence, presenting uncertainty as romance's
defining quality. The categorical wording invites attention to
what Algernon leaves out, such as trust, commitment and the
pleasures of an established relationship.
Explain how a sentence can be an effective comic
generalization without being a reliable guide to relationships.
(Model: Its force can come from exaggerating one attractive
idea while excluding important experiences that would
complicate the claim.)
